Priya CS: Heads-up — prepping Acero QBR for Fri, saw a big embedding spike last week. Can we do a quick cost dry-run and a short enablement ask?
Tom FinOps: sure. drop the rough 30-day numbers and I'll run sims.
Priya CS: 30d baseline: gen 1.2M tokens, emb 4.5M tokens. Estimated spend $3.2k. Last week's spike added ~2.9M embeddings overnight.
Mike SE: I can simulate an operational burst (3x) and a cache/batching case. will need baseline latencies too but can do quick numbers first.
Tom FinOps: running quick sim now, FYI my rough multiplier: embeddings dominate cost.
Mike SE: quick snippet I ran locally: ```python
baseline = {'gen':1200000,'emb':4500000}
burst = {k:int(v*3) for k,v in baseline.items()}
# cost per unit assumptions: gen $0.0008k/token, emb $0.0005k/token (toy numbers)
print(baseline, burst)
```
Tom FinOps: results — with burst, monthly hit ~ $9.6k (rough). If we add a 20% buffer + 7d safety credits for onboarding, recommend asking for a $11.5k monthly commit or retainer.
Priya CS: flagged renewal risk in notes — customer said their A/B stalled because tokens spiked and cost surprised them. We need an enablement session focused on batching + prefix caching + fallback models.
Alex SE: I can run a 45-min enablement demo Tue 10am PT: cover batching config, kv/prefix cache, and model fallbacks. @Priya CS can you confirm invite?
Priya CS: please schedule. Also want a short config/template customers can apply post-demo (one-click-ish). Assign to Maya Docs.
Maya Docs: on it — I'll draft a one-page config template and a snippet for the QBR deck today. capture note: customer reported "inconsistent outputs with quantized model" when switching during spike — adding to the feedback slide.
billing-bot: alert: account Acero exceeded 70% of threshold (threshold=monthly-retainer) at 2025-11-02T14:12:03Z
Priya CS: good catch @billing-bot :eyes: — we'll surface that in the QBR as the trigger for our recommended buffer. Proposed QBR action slide: 1) Baseline + spike sim, 2) Proposed buffer & retainer ask, 3) Enablement schedule + recording, 4) Config template & migration checklist, 5) Feedback log & follow-ups.
Tom FinOps: I'll drop a small chart with baseline vs burst and the recommended dollar buffer. Will have updated numbers + a short note on unit economics by Wed EOD.
Mike SE: I'll prepare a 2-slide tech appendix showing batching knobs and KV-cache impact (samples of expected latency improvements).
Priya CS: thanks — action items captured. Quick wins = enablement + template before QBR, longer term = consider auto-throttle policy and fallback model routing.
Priya CS: thanks everyone :raised_hands:
